Formulation  
Patient with type 2 diabetes developed painful, itchy, cracked dermatitis primarily on her hands over 3-4 months, likely precipitated and perpetuated by occupational exposure to cleaning chemicals and inconsistent glove use. Symptoms interfere with occupational functioning, resulting in recent work absence. Protective factors include patient insight and willingness to engage in protective behaviors (glove use) and prescribed treatment. No mental health concerns or risk issues identified or discussed during consultation.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Contact dermatitis with painful, cracked hand skin impairing function  
- Patient Goal(s): Relief of symptoms; ability to perform work tasks without pain; return to work  
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce skin inflammation and cracking; prevent further irritation; promote skin healing  
- Actions (Patient): Use gloves consistently during cleaning; apply prescribed steroid cream and emollients 3-4 times daily; monitor symptoms; present for follow-up if no improvement or worsening within 1-2 weeks  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe topical steroid and stronger emollient creams; provide education about trigger avoidance; review patient in 1-2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen; arrange follow-up care

- Actions (Clinician/GP): Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Disease process (contact dermatitis), trigger avoidance (glove use), skin care with emollients and steroids, when to seek further review  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing dryness, cracking, pain, spread of rash, bleeding  
- Coping Strategies: Consistent glove use, skin moisturizing regimen
